newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nickel shareholders to meet Sept 8.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel shareholders to meet Sept 8.

text.p: Russian metals producer Norilsk Nickel will hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on September 8, spokesman Yury Oleinikov said on Tuesday.
"According to a decision by the board of directors... the meeting will be held on September 8," Oleinikov told Reuters, without detailing the agenda.

The results of a tender currently under way for a 38 percent stake in Norilsk, the world's biggest producer of palladium and a major producer of platinum, copper and cobalt, will be decided on August 5.

The stake is currently held by Russia's powerful Uneximbank, headed by former first deputy prime minister Vladimir Potanin, under the terms of a controversial government scheme to raise credit from banks in return for stakes in top companies.
The starting price for the stake is 131.6 million ECU, with a $300 million minimum investment requirement.
The winner of the tender will also be responsible for paying the government's debts under the loans for shares scheme, as well as for settling about $70 million in company debts.
Uneximbank has already said it plans to take part in the tender itself.
